Lie Groups and Lie Algebras (2023)

Convener(s)

 
Name: Apoorva Khare R. Venkatesh
Mailing Address: Associate Professor
Department of Mathematics
Indian Institute of Science
Bangalore 560012		 Assistant Professor
Department of Mathematics
Indian Institute of Science
Bangalore 560012
Email: khare at iisc.ac.in rvenkat at iisc.ac.in

Lie groups and Lie algebras are one of the cornerstones of mathematics. They are well-studied in geometry, (harmonic) analysis, representation theory, number theory, string theory, and particle physics, to name several different fields – in addition to featuring in probability theory, control systems, and other areas. This AIS will focus on discussing and developing the basics of topological groups, Lie groups, and Lie algebras, with both their structure and their representations in mind.

The lectures aim to cover the basics of the structure theory of (complex semisimple) Lie algebras, root systems and Dynkin diagrams, topological and Lie groups, the Peter-Weyl theorem, and the correspondence between Lie algebras and Lie groups (via exponentiation). The lectures are meant for an audience of students and postdocs interested in Lie theory. Each lecture (in the morning) is accompanied by a tutorial session (in the afternoon).

Syllabus: 

 

Name of the Speakers with their affiliation.

No. of Lectures

Detailed Syllabus

Ved Datar
Dept. of Maths.
IISc, Bangalore

6

 Review of multivariable calculus including the inverse function theorem, smooth manifolds with examples, smooth functions, partition of unity, tangent spaces and the tangent bundle, vector fields and flows.

Vamsi Pritham Pingali
Dept. of Maths.
IISc, Bangalore

6

 Lie groups with examples (and motivation), left invariant vector fields and the Lie bracket, one parameter subgroups and the exponential map, Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formula, Closed Subgroup Theorem.

Subhojoy Gupta
Dept. of Maths.
IISc, Bangalore

6

 Frobenius theorem and its proof, with commuting flows as a special case; correspondence between Lie subgroups and Lie subalgebras, correspondence between simply-connected Lie groups and finite-dimensional Lie algebras.

Apoorva Khare
Dept. of Maths.
IISc, Bangalore

6

 Structure of semisimple Lie algebras: theorems of Engel and Lie (for nilpotent and solvable Lie algebras), Cartan’s criterion and the Killing form, Weyl’s theorem of complete reducibility, sl(2)-theory, toral subalgebras, root spaces.

R. Venkatesh
Dept. of Maths.
IISc, Bangalore

6

 Root systems, simple bases, classification via Dynkin diagrams, root and weight lattices, isomorphism and existence theorems for semisimple Lie algebras. Theorems of Ado and Levi.

Muna Naik
Dept. of Maths.
HRI, Prayagraj

 6 Compact Lie groups, Lie algebras, representations, weights of representations, Weyl group, highest weight theorem for compact semisimple Lie groups.

References:

  1. V. S. Varadarajan, Lie groups, Lie algebras and their representations, Sringer 1984.
  2. Brian Hall, Lie groups, Lie algebras and representations, Springer 2003.
  3. Barry Simon, Representations of finite and compact groups, AMS 1996.
  4. A. W. Knapp, Representation theory of semismiple Lie groups. An overview based on examples, Princeton university press 2002.
  5. S. Kumaresan S, A course in differential geometry and Lie groups, Texts and Readings in Mathematics, 22. Hindustan Book Agency, New Delhi, 2002.
  6. F. Warner, Foundations of differentiable manifolds and Lie groups, Graduate Texts in Mathematics, 94. Springer-Verlag, New York-Berlin, 1983.
  7. J. E. Humphreys, Introduction to Lie algebras and Representation theory, Springer-Verlag, 1972.
  8. J.-P. Serre, Complex Semisimple Lie Algebras, Springer, 2001.
  9. W. Fulton, and J. Harris, Representation theory, Springer-Verlag. 1991.
  10. Roger Carter, Lie Algebras of Finite and Affine Type, Cambridge University Press, 2010.
